gen-gf-sniglet-fs-synonym: Blunt, rounded and quietly confident. Synonym follows in sans-serif form, a plain stripe of ink with generous openings, and next to Sniglet it feels like a deep breath after a shout.
gen-gf-sniglet-plus-jakarta-sans: Sniglet stops its terminals short of curling back, giving headings a level, unfussy beat. And Plus Jakarta Sans matches that restraint with monoline sans strokes whose curve endings stay well apart, so the two read as precise and sturdy.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-montserrat: A splayed c terminal and tube-like strokes make Tilt Neon instantly recognizable, with a big x-height and short ascenders. Montserrat glides underneath in plain sans form, its oversized e and a counters leaving plenty of white space where the heading is crowded.
gen-megrim-fs-supreme: Megrim draws every stroke as thin and measured as a pipe cleaner, with an angular, futuristic edge. Supreme counters with a thick, heavy-looking sans-serif strip of text, and its letters feel held open rather than curled shut.
gen-mystery-quest-poppins: Nostalgic, with a storybook lean. Mystery Quest has open jaws on its curves and low contrast, while Poppins has none at all, so the loose, rope-like round letters feel modern against the heading's old charm.
gen-flavors-archivo: Whimsical Flavors keeps its diagonals as hefty as its stems, with a towering x-height like a stubby pencil stroke. And Archivo, a plain sans, opens its curves outward with an editorial ease that gives all that heft somewhere to rest.
gen-audiowide-general-sans: Audiowide sets its glyphs like tiles with wide grout lines, with tall lowercase and no thick-thin shifts. General Sans fills the line with its generous x-height, so a plain sans body can be sized up comfortably without crowding.
gen-eater-fs-asap: Thin strokes sit beside moderately weighty stems in Eater, with wide gaps between letters and short ascenders. Asap steps in as the plain sans with low contrast and open arcs, and its body height nearly matching the capitals is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-funnel-display-archivo: Funnel Display draws spaghetti-like strokes in one weight. Archivo, a plain sans, is the one that really earns its keep in text, with curves opening outward and a commanding x-height, while the heading simply performs.
gen-gf-goldman-fs-hind: Goldman's widely set letters have generous clearance and round forms like open parentheses. Hind's sans-serif lowercase nearly matches its capitals, and that steady, string-like stroke with c ends that never turn inward is the pair's strongest quality.
